# Phase One — Release Universe

The Awtsmoos reveals the final mile not as a button but as a river of custody, proof, and public light;
Awtsmoos.com must carry one coherent Chitas vessel from canonical source through mobile sight.

## Mission

Finish Daily Chitas as a native Heichel Ikar experience, improve mobile-first UI/UX on the clean latest-main integration tree, publish the exact tested SHA, activate production through the repository's current release covenant, and verify the public live link.

## Known implementation surface

- Ikar native Chumash source posts and pasuk sections.
- Reusable post-range reference/resolver.
- Dynamic `daily-chitas/chitas-YYYY-MM-DD` reader identity.
- Chabad-calendar-compatible seven-day schedule metadata.
- Simchas Torah/Isru Chag handling.
- Native comments/discussion endpoint.
- Chitas-aware reader previous/next day navigation.
- Guarded native post shell.
- Sunday-through-Shabbos mobile week panel.
- Honest Hebrew Torah / English interface semantics.

## Release graph

`origin/main` -> clean integration worktree -> full-file Chitas transfer -> integration tests -> mobile browser proof -> UX corrections -> complete-file second write -> regression -> commit -> fast-forward main -> push -> bhRelease exact SHA -> public verification -> live link.

## Failure map

- Missing hidden reader dependency could recreate dynamic-reader failure.
- Dirty root staging could absorb unfinished unrelated agents.
- New upstream commit could invalidate a copied owner.
- Calendar fetch could fail in browser while source-range tests still pass.
- Mobile week cards could overflow or bury controls.
- Synthetic discussion identity could diverge after clean integration.
- Production cache generation could mix old/new modules.
- Release activation could target a different SHA than pushed main.
- Public host could serve a healthy shell but fail client-side manifestation.
- Week/date selector could change UI query but not reader post identity.

## Candidate UX improvements

- Stronger Chitas week identity without generic timeline language.
- Compact day cards with weekday, aliyah, source reference, and clear current-day state.
- Sticky or visually anchored study controls on narrow screens without covering Torah.
- Better responsive spacing for 320–430px widths.
- Clear bilingual interface switch labeling that does not imply unavailable English Torah.
- Better focus-visible states and 48px touch targets.
- Date-picker full-width behavior on narrow devices.
- Selected-day card affordance and Today affordance.
- Native reader masthead hierarchy that leaves Torah as visual center.
- Clean source-reference typography and overflow wrapping.

## Completion evidence required

No completion claim until the exact public deployment SHA is observed, public Heichel Chitas grouping is reachable, public dynamic day route is reachable, browser DOM contains the Chitas masthead and native Hebrew Torah, controls fit mobile viewport, no Chabad redirect occurs, discussion endpoint is healthy, and production serves the committed Chitas module generation.
